The Current Care Needs Checklist

What to observe, gather and ask before the next decision.

Mom came home from the hospital “needing more help.” Before anyone decides what that means, make sure you have these in hand. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is a job for this week, not a verdict about Mom.

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you gather and notice. It doesn't tell you what Mom needs or how much. That's for the people who assess her, and for the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've gathered and noticed. The care interview walks you through Mom's situation area by area so nothing important is overlooked, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

Items marked with a dot follow Medicare's discharge planning checklist; the rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  • Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Your Discharge Planning Checklist (CMS publication 11376)
  • Family Caregiver Alliance, Hospital Discharge Planning: A Guide for Families and Caregivers
